The Ramakrishna Mission Sevashrama, Silchar traces its origin to 1915, when the Cachar district was ravaged by a devastating flood and a small group of monks arrived with relief. Their service inspired local youth to form the Ramakrishna Seva Samiti under the late Kamini Kumar Chanda; on 15 February 1939 it was formally affiliated with the Ramakrishna Mission, Belur Math, becoming an official branch centre. Its service work spans education, healthcare (Ma Sarada Charitable Dispensary), rural welfare, mobile medical services and disaster relief. It completed 100 years in 2025, when the newly built Universal Temple of Sri Ramakrishna Paramhamsadeva was inaugurated on 18 March 2025 by Ramakrishna Math/Mission president Swami Gautamananda and Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma (state announced Rs 5 crore for the hospital and Rs 4 crore toward the temple).

name: Ramakrishna Mission Sevashrama (Universal Temple of Sri Ramakrishna)
town_description: Silchar is the second-largest city of Assam and the commercial and educational hub of the Barak Valley, set on the banks of the Barak River. Known as the 'Island of Peace', it is predominantly Bengali-speaking, famous for its grand Durga Puja celebrations and tea estates, and serves as the gateway to southern Assam and the neighbouring states of Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura.

travel.railway: Silchar Junction - close to the city centre campus.
travel.road: On N S Avenue / Mission Road, Silchar; reachable by taxi, auto or city bus.
